project.name: transit-stops-osm-comparison
project.description: This project compares official transit stop data against OSM data and highlights differences between them

tags.description: Used to rate the stop's similarity via bigram matching
For rail-ish modes (rail, tram, light_rail), the OSM stop_point is used to match it to the official stops.
For non-rail-ish modes (bus, ferry), the OSM plattform (or highway=bus_stop or amenity=ferry_terminal) is used to match it to the official stops.
The OSM station is used as fallback match for official stops, if no other matching stops exist.
For non-rail-ish modes (bus, ferry), the OSM plattform (or highway=bus_stop or amenity=ferry_terminal) is used to match it to the official stops.
Nodes with `railway=stop` are considered as potential matches for official stops serving rail-ish modes like tram, rail, light_rail.
Nodes with `railway=tram_stop` are considered as potential matches for official stops serving rail-ish modes like i.e. tram, light_rail.
Nodes with `railway=halt` are considered as fallback matches for official stops serving rail-ish modes like i.e. tram, light_rail, in case there exists no better matching stop/tram_stop/stop_point.

Especially for German and some other European countries stops, ref:IFOPT specifies to official stop ID.
About one thousand OSM stops use `ref:pt_id` instead of `ref:IFOPT`, mainly in some regions of Germany (`de:05*` and Austria. `at:49:*`). Note that we'd recommend to use ref:IFOPT instead.

ref is often stil used to map the local platform code, though local_ref should be used. If it's length is smaller than 3 characters, wie assume it denotes the plattform code and use it to boost matches, if it matches the official platform code.
Used to boost matches, if local_ref matches the official platform code.

Official stops serving routes with route_type 4  (or corresponding extended route_types) are matched against OSM features with `amenity=ferry_terminal` OSM stops (`public_transport=platform`) with `ferry=yes`
route_ref is currently only used for documentary purposes, as it is PTv1 and mostly has been replaced by route relations

OMS stops having a `kerb:approach_aid=yes` are classified as `wheelchair_accessible` in GTFS-sense. However, as the German DELFI-zHV-registry currently does not provide accessiblity information, we don't compare against this yet.

OMS stops having a `wheelchair=yes` are classified as `wheelchair_accessible` in GTFS-sense. However, as the German DELFI-zHV-registry currently does not provide accessiblity information, we don't compare against this yet.
Official stops serving routes with route_type 3 (or corresponding extended route_types) are matched against OSM stops with ` bus=yes` or other non-'rail-ish' stops
Official stops serving routes with route_type 2 (or corresponding extended route_types) are matched against OSM stops with ` train=yes` or other 'rail-ish' stops
Official stops serving routes with route_type 1 (or corresponding extended route_types) are matched against OSM stops with light_rail=yes or other 'rail-ish' stops
Official stops serving routes with route_type 0 (or corresponding extended route_types) are matched against OSM stops with tram=yes (or railway=tram_stop)
Official stops serving routes with route_type 4 (or corresponding extended route_types) are matched against OSM stops with ferry=yes
Official stops serving routes with route_type 7 (or corresponding extended route_types) are matched against OSM stops with funicular=yes
We use `light_rail`, `bus`, `ferry`, `tram`, `train`. relations to deduce stop order. Names of preceding and subsequent stops are used evaluated to detect direction issues.
